nodes.label: ApiError (retryable / retryAfterMs / requestId)
nodes.rationale: Network and timeout failures reject with ApiError (code NETWORK_ERROR or TIMEOUT, status 0) instead of a raw TypeError, and hosts branch on retryable rather than on status. The server SDK behaves identically so client and server errors are interchangeable.

nodes.label: createNotificationsClient (requestId -> x-request-id)
nodes.rationale: Server SDK factory takes an optional requestId sent as x-request-id, giving client and server the same ApiError shape and correlatable requests.

nodes.label: InboxError
nodes.rationale: Gains retryable and requestId so load failures expose the same retry decision surface as ApiError.

nodes.label: NotificationBellUnavailable
nodes.rationale: Renders the same error bell for a host that cannot mount the live bell yet, so a missing backend still shows the icon plus warning triangle rather than disappearing.

nodes.label: onError Callback
nodes.rationale: Reports every failure to the host for logs and metrics, with a stream outage reported once per outage.

nodes.label: TokenError
nodes.rationale: Lets a host throw a token failure carrying its status: 501, 401 or 404 stops the bell permanently, while 503 is retried.

nodes.label: publish channels Non-Empty Validation
nodes.rationale: publish takes channels as a non-empty list matching the server, which rejects an empty one; omitting the field uses server defaults, and a runtime-built list must keep at least one channel.

nodes.label: tokenUrl Host Token Endpoint Prop
nodes.rationale: The widget calls the host token endpoint itself so a host does not have to write fetch and envelope parsing; getToken stays supported for hosts that prefer supplying tokens.

nodes.label: Live Bell Failure Recovery and Reconnect Schedule
nodes.norm_label: live bell failure recovery and reconnect schedule
nodes.rationale: Recovery is retried rather than terminal: a token refresh that fails mid-request is retried instead of reported as permanent refusal; a stream that opens and drops keeps backing off and reports its outage once, resetting only after 30s of uptime; a stream silent for 90s or unanswered in 10s is cut and reconnected; Retry-After is capped at 5 minutes; the token request bypasses the browser cache; a failed start/refresh/load backs off while offline or the tab is hidden.

nodes.label: bellLabel / bellAnnouncement Client Exports
nodes.rationale: Exported from the client so the trigger label and live announcement are literally shared by every port instead of duplicated per framework.

nodes.label: Vue, Vanilla and Angular Bells (v0.2.0)
nodes.rationale: Each non-React port binds the same client store as the React bell and renders the same UI, props and DOM hooks, so hosts switch frameworks without a behavior or markup fork. New subpath entries /vue, /vanilla and /angular ship their own stylesheets, while ./styles.css still points at the React sheet so existing imports keep working.

nodes.label: React Example Demo Page
nodes.rationale: Vite-style module shell: a bare #root div mounted by /src/main.tsx, so the React demo owns all markup from JS.

nodes.label: Vanilla Example Demo Page
nodes.rationale: Static header layout with a dedicated #bell mount node, showing the vanilla port attaches the bell next to plain page markup loaded by /src/main.ts.

nodes.label: Vue Example Demo Page
nodes.rationale: Same #root module-shell shape as the React demo, mounted by /src/main.ts, keeping the port demos structurally comparable.

nodes.label: Optional Vue/Angular/Lucide-Angular Peers
nodes.rationale: Vue, Angular and Lucide-Angular are declared optional peers so React apps install nothing new when adding the package.
